new_entities.name: Creatine monohydrate supplementation
new_entities.description: Oral creatine monohydrate supplementation used to support training adaptations and high-intensity exercise performance.

new_entities.name: Cognitive performance under sleep deprivation
new_entities.description: Attention, memory, processing speed, or related cognitive performance measured during acute sleep deprivation.

edges.effect_quant: Small controlled trials suggest creatine can blunt the usual decline in vigilance, memory, or processing speed during acute sleep deprivation, but the evidence base remains tiny.
edges.population: healthy adults undergoing acute partial or total sleep deprivation
edges.mechanism: Sleep deprivation impairs cognitive performance partly through energetic stress in the brain. Creatine may buffer some of that deficit by increasing high-energy phosphate availability, which fits both the psychomotor findings and the spectroscopy studies showing altered phosphocreatine and ATP-related measures after dosing.
edges.summary: There is a plausible and repeatedly positive signal here, but it is early-stage rather than settled. Small placebo-controlled studies suggest creatine can partially preserve cognition during sleep deprivation, yet the evidence is not broad enough to rate at the same confidence level as its exercise-performance uses.
edges.caveats: The literature is limited to small short-term experiments, with one later paper reanalyzing a previously published cohort. Effects may depend on the dosing strategy, the type of sleep loss, and the specific cognitive task measured.

evidence.notes: Single dose creatine improves cognitive performance and induces changes in cerebral high energy phosphates during sleep deprivation.
Effect of creatine supplementation and sleep deprivation, with mild exercise, on cognitive and psychomotor performance, mood state, and plasma concentrations of catecholamines and cortisol.
Hemispheric asymmetry in high-energy phosphate consumption during sleep-deprivation is balanced by creatine.
